title: DECISION: No enums in UAPI — strings for algo IDs, #define for closed sets
description: crypto2dev_ioctl.h contains no typedef enum or anonymous enum. Algorithm identifiers are strings (e.g., 'cbc(aes)'). Small permanently-closed operation sets use #define integer constants. Adding an enum to the UAPI would freeze the value space at the current algorithm set — every new algorithm requires a header change and recompile of all callers including out-of-tree modules and userspace binaries. Strings have no such constraint. A reviewer who says 'use enum for type safety' is proposing ABI debt. The answer is no.
